name: Māyā the swindler
description: Māyā, the great swindler with the noose of the three qualities, who appears in every house in a different form — wealth, the goddess, the idol, the pilgrim-water — and binds all creatures.

name: Gold and woman (kanak-kāminī)
description: The Sants' paired snares of wealth and sexual desire, named as the two forms of māyā that bind the renunciant and the householder alike; recorded faithfully as the verses state it (see cpt:women-sant-baul).

sources.ref: Māyā kau aṅg; Kāmī nar kau aṅg

name: The unruly mind
description: The restless mind that wanders while the lips recite, runs after the senses like an elephant or thief, and makes defeat and victory; in Sant Mat the agent of Kāl.

name: Delusion (bhram)
description: The delusion of sect, scripture and outward religion — Hindu and Turk each certain of his own way — and of taking the mind's creations for the real.

name: Garb and hypocrisy (bheṣ, pākhaṇḍ)
description: Taking the ascetic's garb, marks and feats for holiness; the yogī dyes his clothes but not his mind.

equivalents.note: The Sant critique targets all sectarian garb, not only false ascetics.

name: The five thieves
description: Lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride, which rob the house of the body; the guru frees the disciple from them (Sahajobāī).

equivalents.note: Five of the six enemies (envy omitted).

name: Six enemies (ṣaḍ-ripu; Bāul chay ripu)
description: Desire, anger, greed, delusion, pride and envy, which the Bāul and Sahajiyā songs name as the enemies to be mastered before the Man can be held.

name: Pride of caste (jāti-abhimān)
description: The brahmin's pride of birth and the whole world's question 'what caste?', which the Sants and Bāuls treat as an obstacle to the Lord.

equivalents.note: Pride of family/lineage; the Sant critique extends to the whole caste order.

name: Book-learning without love
description: Reading books till death without becoming wise; speaking of what is written on paper instead of what is seen; for Bāuls, reliance on scripture (anumān).

name: Dependence on inference and hearsay (anumān)
description: Accepting scripture, heaven and the gods of the books without verification in the living body.

name: Ego (āpā, 'I')
description: The 'I' that leaves no room in the narrow lane of love; the self that must be erased (āpā meṭe) for Hari to be.

name: Kāma (lust, desire for one's own pleasure)
description: Desire for one's own pleasure, the downward current; for the Sahajiyā not to be suppressed but refined into prema, for the Bāuls to be mastered before practice — and the danger into which the unqualified fall.

name: Hope and craving (āśā, tṛṣṇā)
description: Hope in the world and craving, which keep the soul returning; the jīvan-mṛtak is one who has given up hope in the world.

name: Bad company (kusaṅg)
description: Company of the worldly, the hypocrite and the unrestrained, which undoes practice; its remedy is satsaṅg.

name: The snare of Kāl
description: Kāl (Nirañjan, the negative power) keeps souls bound in the three worlds by karma, māyā and false religion, and sends false teachers; freed only by the true Name/Sant Satguru.

name: Powers as a snare (riddhi-siddhi)
description: Yogic powers and feats, and attachment to inner lights and sounds for their own sake, which distract from the Lord.
